title: Graph-R1: Towards Agentic GraphRAG Framework via End-to-end Reinforcement Learning

analysis.tldr: Graph-R1 turns GraphRAG retrieval into a learned multi-turn agent–graph interaction and optimizes the whole retrieval/reasoning trajectory with reinforcement learning.
analysis.problem: Conventional GraphRAG often performs fixed one-shot retrieval and leaves long-context reasoning to prompting, so the model does not learn a retrieval policy over graph structure.
analysis.core_idea: Construct a lightweight knowledge hypergraph, expose retrieval as a sequential interaction, and train the agent end to end using outcome-based rewards.
analysis.agent_loop: Reason → choose graph retrieval action → observe graph evidence → update state → repeat → answer
analysis.retrieval_design: The graph is an interactive retrieval environment rather than a single precomputed context expansion; the retrieval trajectory is directly optimized by RL.
analysis.evidence: The paper reports improvements in reasoning accuracy, retrieval efficiency, and generation quality on standard RAG datasets; the bootstrap note has not yet re-checked the complete experimental tables and ablations.
analysis.why_it_matters: It makes the retrieval trajectory itself a policy-learning object, connecting GraphRAG with end-to-end agent optimization rather than treating graph retrieval as a static preprocessing stage.
limitations: Outcome-level RL can provide weak credit assignment for intermediate retrieval actions.
The bootstrap note has not yet been upgraded to full-paper verification.
